meta.description: Daily tracking state for F-1/SEVP/DS-2019 policy monitoring, focused on relevance to a Virginia Tech student who may need an extra semester to finish their degree.

items.title: DHS Final Rule: Fixed Time Period of Admission & Extension of Stay (ends Duration of Status) for F, J, I nonimmigrants
items.summary: DHS published a final rule (doc. 2026-14439) on Jul 17, 2026, ending open-ended Duration of Status for F-1 students, effective Sep 15, 2026. Students get a fixed 'Admit Until Date' capped at 4 years (24 months for language programs); anyone needing more time must file Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) with USCIS in addition to the existing DSO SEVIS extension. A timely-filed EOS gives up to 240 days of authorized stay while pending.
items.notes: No lawsuit had been filed and no Congressional Review Act disapproval resolution had passed as of this run; NAFSA has publicly opposed the rule but litigation remains anticipatory only. SEVP has scheduled a stakeholder webinar for Mon, Aug 31, 2026, 2-3pm ET to walk through the rule (per Study in the States listing, relayed via secondary source since studyinthestates.dhs.gov could not be fetched directly this run).

items.title: USCIS Policy Alert PA-2026-05: officers may deny incomplete filings without issuing an RFE/NOID first
items.summary: Effective Aug 5, 2026, USCIS updated Policy Manual guidance so adjudicators may, at their discretion, deny a benefit request lacking required initial evidence or failing to establish eligibility without first issuing an RFE or NOID, and may set RFE response deadlines shorter than the prior 12-week norm. Directly relevant to F-1 students filing Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) or I-765 under the new fixed-admission-period regime: an incomplete EOS package can now be denied outright with no chance to cure.
items.notes: Could not reach uscis.gov/policy-manual directly this run (network egress to uscis.gov is blocked in this environment) to pull the actual Policy Alert PA-2026-05 text/citation. Will keep retrying uscis.gov each run to move this to Confirmed.

items.title: DHS regulatory review of OPT / STEM OPT (RIN 1653-AA97) — no NPRM published yet
items.summary: DHS confirmed in a Jan 9, 2026 letter it is re-evaluating the scope and duration of OPT and STEM OPT, with a rulemaking entry (RIN 1653-AA97) in the Spring 2026 Unified Regulatory Agenda. As of this run, no Notice of Proposed Rulemaking has been published in the Federal Register; secondary reporting suggests a proposal is not expected before early 2027. Relevant because many students planning an extra semester are also relying on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT timing.
items.notes: Could not reach reginfo.gov or federalregister.gov directly this run to confirm the RIN 1653-AA97 unified-agenda entry text. No OPT/STEM OPT NPRM exists yet to cite as of 2026-08-10. Will keep watching for actual NPRM publication.
